DNA‐stable 5H1 and 10H1 cells were established from 2H1 cells by repeated exposure to demecolcide, but DNA‐unstable 8H1 and 4H1 cells were not.
DNA‐stable 5H1 (ES) cell polyploidization using demecolchicine led to the establishment of DNA‐unstable 10H1 (ES), which reverted to 2H1 (ES).
decaploid H2 (ES) cells were DNA‐stable and had a higher growth rate than 5H1 and 10H1 cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the stability of cell ploidy in long‐term cell culture.
the establishment and characterization of decaploid H‐1 mouse embryonal stem (ES) cells from DNA‐stable 5H1 mouse ES cells, and with a discussion of ploidy stability.
the establishment and characterization of 10H1 cells and the comparison of DNA stability between 5H1 and 10H1.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DNA content of 10H1 cells is stable.
the ploidy stability of 5H1 and 10H1 cells is determined by the ploidy stability and DNA stability of their parental cells.
DNA‐stable 5H1, 2H1, and 1H1 cells are all derived from the same diploid stem cell line.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ploidy stability of H1 (ES), which is an important characteristic of this cell line, is determined by the DNA content.
DNA stability of H1 (ES‐derived) cells is determined by ploidy.
ploidy stability is determined by the number of centrosomes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 10H1 cells were found to be DNA unstable.
DNA‐unstable cells can undergo polyploidization, and the resulting cells can become DNA‐stable.
the DNA‐unstable 10H1 cells were derived from the DNA‐stable 5H1 and 2H1 cells, but not from the DNA‐unstabe 4H1 or 8H1, suggesting that DNA stability is determined by ploidy level.
